sections.heading: Broken down, flat, or damaged.
sections.body: Our 24 hour tow service can get you out of a jam when you need it. If your vehicle breaks down or becomes disabled in an accident, call the 24 hour number and a licensed tow truck driver is sent to your location.

sections.heading: Wreckers and emergency towing.
sections.body: Tow trucks, wreckers and emergency towing across Dallas. Emergency work is the bulk of what we do, which is why the line is answered around the clock rather than during office hours.

sections.heading: The location matters as much as the vehicle.
sections.body: A car on a driveway and the same car on the shoulder of a highway are different jobs. Traffic, barriers, soft ground and low clearance all change which truck can actually reach it and how long the recovery takes. Saying where you are precisely — the road, the direction of travel, the nearest exit — gets the right truck moving sooner than a ZIP code does.

sections.heading: Location is the part people get wrong.
sections.body: A street name is enough in a neighborhood and close to useless on a highway, where the same road runs for miles in both directions. Exit numbers, mile markers, the last sign you passed and which direction you were traveling all narrow it down far faster. If your phone can share a pin, that settles it outright. The second thing worth having ready is where the vehicle is going, because a tow to a shop across town and a tow to your driveway are different jobs to quote and to plan. And if the car will not shift out of park, the keys are missing, or it is boxed in, say so on the call rather than when the driver is standing next to it.

faqs.q: Flatbed or a regular tow truck?
faqs.a: A flatbed carries the vehicle with all four wheels off the road, which is what you want for all-wheel drive, low ground clearance, a car with damaged wheels, or anything you would rather not have rolling behind a truck. A conventional tow truck lifts one end and is quicker to hook up. Say what you are driving and dispatch can pick.

faqs.q: Can you get to a vehicle in a parking garage?
faqs.a: Low clearance is the deciding factor and it is worth mentioning on the call, because a flatbed that cannot get under the entrance is a wasted trip for both of us. If you know the height limit posted at the entrance, that single number answers most of the question.

pages.heading: Roadside assistance across Dallas.
pages.intro: Not every problem needs a tow. Often the quicker answer is getting the vehicle running again where it sits.
pages.seoTitle: Roadside Assistance Dallas TX | 24 Hour Towing Dallas
pages.seoDescription: Roadside assistance in Dallas, Texas — tire changes, jumpstarts and help getting a disabled vehicle back on the road, 24 hours a day.

sections.heading: Back on the road, not on a truck.
sections.body: From having a tire changed to jumpstarting your car, roadside assistance is about getting the vehicle moving again rather than hauling it somewhere. When that is the faster fix, it is the cheaper one too.

sections.heading: Dispatched from the same 24 hour line.
sections.body: Roadside calls run through the same dispatch as the tow trucks, so there is one number to remember whichever of the two you turn out to need.

sections.heading: Get clear of the traffic side.
sections.body: If you are on a live carriageway, the safest place is usually out of the vehicle and behind a barrier, not sitting in the driver's seat. If the car is somewhere you cannot safely leave it, say so when you call — it changes how urgently the job is treated.

sections.heading: Some problems move with the vehicle.
sections.body: Roadside work is for things that can be put right where the car sits: a flat with a usable spare, a dead battery, an empty tank, keys locked inside. Those are quick and nothing has to be transported. Other problems only look like roadside jobs. A flat with no spare, a shredded sidewall, a car that starts and immediately dies again, or anything involving the transmission means the vehicle has to move regardless. Knowing which one you have before a truck is dispatched saves a trip that cannot fix anything. If you are not sure, describe the symptoms on the call — what happened, what it sounded like, whether anything still works — and dispatch can usually tell which way it will go.

faqs.q: Is roadside help cheaper than a tow?
faqs.a: Usually, because nothing is being transported — but only when the problem is actually fixable at the roadside. A flat tire with a usable spare, a dead battery, or an empty tank are roadside jobs. A failed transmission is not. If it turns out the vehicle has to move, it is better to know that before a truck is dispatched.

faqs.q: What if I have no spare tire?
faqs.a: Then the vehicle needs to move rather than be fixed where it sits, because there is nothing to fit. Plenty of newer cars ship with a sealant kit instead of a spare, which handles a puncture but not a sidewall tear or a blowout. Check before you call — it changes which truck comes out.

pages.heading: Battery jumpstarts and replacement.
pages.intro: A dead battery does not have to end the day. We can jump it where it sits, or replace it and have you moving again.
pages.seoTitle: Car Battery Jumpstart & Replacement Dallas TX | 24 Hour Towing Dallas
pages.seoDescription: Car battery jumpstarts and replacement in Dallas, Texas. Jumper boxes mean a dead battery can be started wherever the car is parked.

sections.heading: Two ways out of a dead battery.
sections.body: As one of our roadside assistance services, we can replace or jumpstart your car's dead battery. A licensed driver is sent out and will either provide a jumpstart or fit a new battery, changing it out on the spot.

sections.kicker: Why it matters who does it
sections.heading: Jumping a car wrong can cost you an ECU.
sections.body: We are equipped with jumper boxes, so a dead battery can be started regardless of where the car is parked. It is worth saying that jumping a vehicle has to be done correctly — done incorrectly it can damage the car’s computer, which is a far more expensive problem than the battery was.

sections.kicker: When a jump will not hold
sections.heading: A battery that dies twice is not a flat battery.
sections.body: If a car starts on a jump and dies again shortly after, the battery is usually not the fault — it is more often the alternator failing to recharge it. Worth knowing before paying for a replacement battery that will be flat again by the end of the week.

sections.heading: What happens after the jump tells you.
sections.body: A jump start puts enough charge in to turn the engine over. What happens next is the diagnosis. If the car runs and keeps running, the battery was drained — lights left on, a door not shut, a short trip that never let it recover — and it will likely charge back up as you drive. If it starts and then dies again within minutes, the charging system is not doing its job, and a second jump buys the same few minutes as the first. Either way, get it somewhere it can be tested rather than relying on repeat jumps. A battery that has been run flat several times rarely comes back to full health even once the underlying fault is found.

faqs.q: Will a jump start fix it, or do I need a battery?
faqs.a: A jump gets the engine running. Whether it stays running is the real test: if the car starts and then dies again shortly after, the battery is not holding charge or the alternator is not charging it, and a second jump only buys the same few minutes. A jump that holds usually means the battery was drained rather than dead.

pages.heading: We buy junk cars.
pages.intro: If the vehicle is not worth recovering, we will take it off your hands rather than tow it somewhere you have to deal with it again.
pages.seoTitle: We Buy Junk Cars Dallas TX | 24 Hour Towing Dallas
pages.seoDescription: Junk car removal in Dallas, Texas. We buy junk cars and haul them away, so a vehicle that is not worth repairing stops being your problem.

sections.kicker: When it is the right call
sections.heading: Some vehicles are not worth the tow.
sections.body: A car that will cost more to repair than it is worth does not need recovering to a shop. Removing it is usually the cheaper end to the story, and it clears the driveway or the yard at the same time.

sections.heading: Title and location.
sections.body: The two things that decide whether a junk car can be collected are whether you hold the title and whether the vehicle can be reached by a truck. A car with no title, or one boxed in behind two others in a garage, is a different job — not impossible, just worth mentioning on the phone rather than on the day.

sections.heading: Whether it rolls matters more than whether it runs.
sections.body: Non-running is normal — that is most of what gets collected. The questions that actually change the equipment are different ones. Does it still roll, or are the wheels gone or seized? Is it reachable, or is it behind a gate, up against a fence, or boxed in by other vehicles? Has it sunk into soft ground after sitting through a few seasons? A car that can be winched straight onto a bed is a simple job; one that has to be dragged out of a back yard past two other vehicles is not, and finding that out on arrival helps nobody. Mention ownership paperwork on the call too, since that usually needs to be sorted before anything moves.

sections.heading: What a junk car is worth to us.
sections.body: A junk car is valued on what can still be done with it, which is mostly about what it is and what is still on it. Make, model and year matter, and so does whether it is complete — engine, transmission, catalytic converter and wheels all still in place — or has already been picked over. A car that rolls and can be loaded easily is a simpler collection than one that has to be dragged out. Describe it honestly on the call and the answer you get will be one that holds when the truck arrives.

sections.heading: Sign the title, then tell the state.
sections.body: In Texas, selling a vehicle — junk or not — means signing the title over to the buyer. Once it is gone, file a Vehicle Transfer Notification with the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles. That is the step people skip, and it is the one that stops later tickets, tolls or fees attached to the car from coming back to you. If the title is lost, a certified copy can be requested from the TxDMV; mention it on the call either way.

sections.heading: Empty it out, and take the toll tag.
sections.body: Go through the glove box, the trunk, under the seats and the door pockets before collection day. Take out garage door openers, registration papers and anything with your name on it. In Dallas the one most often forgotten is the toll tag on the windshield: remove it or deactivate it with the issuer, or the next person to drive that car through a toll plaza does it on your account.

pages.ctaHeadline: Got a car to get rid of?

faqs.q: Does the car need to run?
faqs.a: No. Non-running, wrecked, flood-damaged and long-dead vehicles are all removable. What matters more than whether it starts is whether it can be reached and whether it rolls — a car with no wheels, or one boxed in behind other vehicles, needs different equipment. Mention that when you call.

faqs.q: What should I take out of the car before it is collected?
faqs.a: Everything personal — glove box, trunk, under the seats — plus garage door openers and any papers with your name or address. Remove or deactivate the toll tag on the windshield. Once the car is gone, getting anything back out of it is not realistic.

faqs.q: What do I do after the car is gone?
faqs.a: File a Vehicle Transfer Notification with the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles so the state knows the car is no longer yours, and cancel the insurance on it. Those two steps close it out properly and stop anything tied to the car from following you afterward.

pages.seoDescription: Tow trucks and roadside assistance in Arlington, Texas, dispatched 24 hours a day from the same Dallas operation.

sections.heading: Arlington is on our patch.
sections.body: The Dallas–Fort Worth corridor is one service area in practice, and Arlington sits in the middle of it. Towing, roadside assistance, jumpstarts and junk car removal all run from the same dispatch.

sections.heading: Arlington is a drive, and that is worth saying.
sections.body: Arlington sits between Dallas and Fort Worth, so a truck coming from Dallas covers real distance to reach it. That is fine for a planned tow or a junk car collection. For something urgent it is worth asking what is actually nearest, because the fastest truck is not always ours and saying so is cheaper than a long wait.

sections.heading: The same services, the same number.
sections.body: Towing, roadside assistance, jump starts, tire changes, lockouts, fuel and junk car collection all run in Arlington exactly as they do in Dallas. The only practical difference is the drive, which matters for something urgent and not at all for something planned.

sections.heading: Dallas-based, Arlington covered.
sections.body: Arlington sits inside the service area, and the base is in Dallas. That is worth stating plainly, because towing directories are full of suburb pages implying a yard around the corner that does not exist, and the difference shows up in how long a truck takes to reach you. If timing is what decides your call, ask about it directly rather than reading it off a page. What the coverage does mean is a single number for the metro: the same dispatch handles Arlington, Dallas and the suburbs between them, so you are not working through a list trying to find who covers where you happen to have broken down.

faqs.q: Are you actually based in Arlington?
faqs.a: No — the base is in Dallas and Arlington is within the service area. That is worth saying plainly, because a local address on every suburb page is a thing towing directories do and it is not true. Where the truck starts from matters for how long it takes, so ask on the call if timing is the deciding factor.

pages.heading: Wrecker and heavy-duty towing in Dallas.
pages.intro: For the vehicles a standard tow truck cannot take — box trucks, buses, RVs and tractor units — dispatched on the same 24-hour line.
pages.seoTitle: Wrecker Service Dallas TX | Heavy Duty Towing | 24 Hour Towing Dallas
pages.seoDescription: 24 hour wrecker service and heavy-duty towing in Dallas, Texas. Box trucks, buses, RVs and tractor units recovered and moved, day or night.

sections.heading: Weight is what decides it.
sections.body: A standard tow truck is built for cars and light pickups. Once the vehicle is a box truck, a bus, a motorhome or a tractor unit, the job needs a wrecker: heavier boom, heavier winch, and a chassis rated to lift it without being dragged around by it. Putting the wrong truck on a heavy recovery is how both vehicles end up damaged.

sections.heading: Three things decide which truck we send.
sections.body: What the vehicle is, roughly what it weighs, and what the access is like. A tractor unit on a shoulder and the same unit in a soft yard are different jobs needing different equipment. Getting that right on the phone is the difference between one truck arriving and two.

sections.heading: Heavy breakdowns do not keep hours.
sections.body: Commercial vehicles break down on schedules, which means at night and at weekends as often as not. Wrecker work runs through the same 24-hour dispatch as everything else, so there is one number whichever kind of truck you turn out to need.

sections.heading: Where the vehicle sits changes the job.
sections.body: Weight decides which truck, but access decides how the recovery is done. The same tractor unit on a shoulder and in a soft yard are two different jobs: one is a straightforward hookup, the other may need winching before anything can be lifted, and possibly room to work that is not there. Overhead clearance, the surface underfoot, how much space there is to bring a truck alongside, and whether the vehicle can roll at all are all worth describing on the call. It is the difference between one truck arriving prepared and a second having to be sent. If you can send a photograph of the position, that answers more than a description usually can.

sections.heading: What the word actually means.
sections.body: People say wrecker and tow truck as if they were the same thing, and for a car they nearly are. The difference shows up with weight. A light-duty wrecker handles cars and pickups; medium and heavy-duty wreckers carry bigger booms, stronger winches and rotating or underlift gear built for vehicles that weigh many times what a car does. When you call asking for a wrecker in Dallas, the useful answer is not yes or no but which class of truck the job needs — and that comes from what the vehicle is, not from the word used to ask.

sections.heading: Big vehicles break down in awkward places.
sections.body: A box truck or a bus rarely stops somewhere convenient. On I-35E, I-30, I-635 or the Central Expressway it is usually on a narrow shoulder with traffic running past, and the recovery has to be planned around that rather than around the vehicle alone. Tell dispatch the road, the direction of travel and the nearest exit or mile marker, and whether the vehicle is blocking a lane. If police are already on scene, say so — it changes how the truck is positioned and how quickly the lane can be cleared.

sections.heading: A loaded truck is a heavier job.
sections.body: The weight that matters is the weight on the ground today, not the empty weight on the paperwork. A box truck full of freight, an RV with full tanks, or a trailer still hitched all change what is needed to lift and move it safely. If the cargo can be taken off first, that can make the tow simpler; if it cannot, say what it is and roughly how much there is, so the right truck comes out the first time.

faqs.q: Is heavy hauling your main business?
faqs.a: No — most of the work is cars and light pickups, and that is what the fleet is built around. Heavy and wrecker work is genuinely offered rather than advertised for its own sake, which is worth saying plainly: if you are moving a tractor unit, describe the job properly on the call so dispatch can tell you straight away whether it is one we should take.

faqs.q: What should I have ready when I call about a heavy vehicle?
faqs.a: What the vehicle is, roughly what it weighs, whether it still rolls, and what the access is like — surface underfoot, overhead clearance, and how much room there is to bring a truck alongside. A photograph of how it is sitting answers more than a description usually can. Those details decide which truck comes out, and getting them right is the difference between one truck arriving prepared and a second having to follow.

faqs.q: Can you tow an RV or motorhome?
faqs.a: Yes, it is one of the vehicles wrecker service exists for. Say on the call how long it is, whether it is a drivable motorhome or a towable trailer, and whether the tanks are full, because all three change the truck that is sent. If it has slide-outs, make sure they are retracted before the truck arrives if you can.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a wrecker and a tow truck?
faqs.a: For a car, very little — the words get used interchangeably. For a heavy vehicle the difference is the equipment: a heavy-duty wrecker has the boom, winch and underlift capacity to raise a bus or tractor unit, which a standard tow truck simply does not. Describe the vehicle and dispatch will work out which one the job needs.

sections.heading: Some vehicles should not be towed on two wheels.
sections.body: A wheel-lift tow picks up one end of the car and rolls it on the other. For most front-wheel-drive cars that is fine. For all-wheel-drive and many four-wheel-drive vehicles, rolling on two wheels can damage the drivetrain, and the repair costs far more than the tow did. A flatbed carries the whole vehicle on the deck, so nothing turns that should not.

sections.heading: Low, damaged, or worth a lot.
sections.body: Ask for a flatbed for all-wheel-drive vehicles, low sports cars that would scrape on a ramp angle, cars with damaged wheels or suspension after an accident, classics, and anything you would rather not see bounced along the road behind a truck. If you are not sure, say what the vehicle is and dispatch can tell you.

sections.heading: It does not need to start.
sections.body: A flatbed is often the simplest way to move a car that will not run, because the winch pulls it up onto the deck rather than relying on it to drive on. Say whether the wheels still turn and whether the steering is locked, since both change how it is loaded.

sections.heading: What helps dispatch send the right truck.
sections.body: The make and model settles most of it, because that tells dispatch whether the vehicle is all-wheel drive and roughly how low it sits. After that, the useful details are where the car is and what is around it. A flatbed is longer than a wheel-lift truck and needs room to tilt the deck, so a tight parking garage, a low ceiling, or a car wedged between two others is worth mentioning up front. Say where it is going too. A flatbed tow to a shop across Dallas and one to your driveway are planned differently, and knowing both ends of the trip is what makes the quote you hear on the phone the one you pay.

faqs.q: Does my car need a flatbed?
faqs.a: If it is all-wheel drive, very low, damaged at the wheels or suspension, or something you would not want rolling on the road, yes. Most front-wheel-drive cars can be towed either way. Tell dispatch the make and model and they will say which.

faqs.q: Can a flatbed get into a parking garage?
faqs.a: Often not. A flatbed is long and needs room and height to tilt the deck. If the car is in a garage or a tight lot, say so on the call — it may need moving out with a smaller truck first.

pages.heading: Car lockout service in Dallas.
pages.intro: Keys locked inside the car — opened without damage to the door, the lock or the glass.
pages.seoTitle: Car Lockout Service Dallas TX | 24 Hour Towing Dallas
pages.seoDescription: Locked out of your car in Dallas? 24 hour lockout service to open your vehicle without damaging the door, lock or window.

sections.heading: Getting you back in without breaking anything.
sections.body: Most lockouts are keys left on the seat or in the ignition. The job is to open the door with the right tools, not to force it. Done properly, the car is opened without marks on the paint, damage to the weather seal, or a broken window.

sections.heading: Check the other doors first.
sections.body: It sounds obvious, but a back door or the trunk release is sometimes left unlocked, and it is worth trying every door before waiting on a truck. If there is a spare key at home and someone can bring it, that may be quicker still.

sections.heading: A child or a pet inside is an emergency.
sections.body: If a child or an animal is locked in the car, especially in Texas heat, call 911 first. Do not wait for a lockout service. Emergency services will treat it as the urgent situation it is.

sections.heading: What to have ready.
sections.body: Say where the car is, what the make and model are, and where the keys are — on the seat, in the ignition, or lost entirely. That last one matters: if the keys are inside, opening the door solves it; if they are lost, opening the door does not get the car started, and you may need a locksmith or a tow to the dealer instead. Be ready to show that the car is yours once it is open, with an ID that matches the registration or insurance card inside. Nobody should open a car for someone who cannot show it belongs to them, and a lockout service that does not ask is not one to trust.

faqs.q: Will opening the car damage it?
faqs.a: It should not. Lockout tools are designed to open the door without forcing the lock or breaking glass. That is the whole point of calling someone rather than trying it with a coat hanger.

faqs.q: What if I have lost the keys altogether?
faqs.a: Then opening the door only solves half of it. Say so on the call — the car may need a locksmith to cut a new key or a tow to the dealer, and it is better to know that before anyone drives out.

pages.heading: Out of gas in Dallas? Fuel brought to you.
pages.intro: Enough fuel delivered to get you to a station, so running out of gas does not turn into a tow.
pages.seoTitle: Emergency Fuel Delivery Dallas TX | 24 Hour Towing Dallas
pages.seoDescription: Ran out of gas in Dallas? 24 hour emergency fuel delivery brings enough fuel to get you to the nearest station.

sections.heading: Enough to get you to a pump.
sections.body: Fuel delivery is not a fill-up. A driver brings enough fuel to get the car running and to the nearest gas station, where you fill it properly. It is the cheaper alternative to towing a car that has nothing wrong with it except an empty tank.

sections.heading: Say which one the car takes.
sections.body: It sounds basic, but it is the one detail that has to be right. Putting the wrong fuel in a tank causes far more trouble than running out did. Tell dispatch whether the vehicle takes regular gasoline or diesel.

sections.heading: Get somewhere safe first.
sections.body: If the car is still rolling when the gauge hits empty, get it off the highway — onto the shoulder as far as it will go, or better, into a parking lot or onto a side street. Turn the hazards on. Stay in the vehicle with your seatbelt on if you are stopped on a busy road, or out of it and well away from traffic if it is safe to do so.

sections.kicker: When fuel is not the fix
sections.heading: If it still will not start.
sections.body: Sometimes the car runs out of fuel and something else turns out to be wrong as well, or the gauge read empty because of a fault rather than an empty tank. If the car will not start after fuel goes in, a modern engine may need a few tries to prime the fuel lines — but if it still will not catch, do not keep cranking until the battery dies too. At that point it is a tow or a jump, not more fuel, and since it is the same dispatch, the driver who is already there can tell you which.

faqs.q: How much fuel do you bring?
faqs.a: Enough to get you to the nearest gas station, not a full tank. It is meant to get you moving, then you fill up properly at a pump.

faqs.q: Can you bring diesel?
faqs.a: Ask when you call and say clearly which fuel the vehicle takes. Getting that right matters more than anything else on the call.

pages.heading: Flat tire changes in Dallas.
pages.intro: Your spare fitted at the roadside, so a flat tire does not become a tow.
pages.seoTitle: Flat Tire Change Dallas TX | Roadside Tire Service | 24 Hour Towing Dallas
pages.seoDescription: Flat tire in Dallas? 24 hour roadside tire change service fits your spare so you can keep driving. Towing if the spare is missing.

sections.heading: Spare on, flat in the trunk.
sections.body: A driver comes out, jacks the car up safely, takes the flat off and puts your spare on. It is a simple job on a quiet street and a far less simple one on a highway shoulder with traffic passing a few feet away, which is the main reason to have someone else do it.

sections.heading: The spare has to be there, and it has to hold air.
sections.body: A tire change depends on the car having a usable spare. Many newer cars come with an inflation kit instead, and spares that have sat in the trunk for years are often flat themselves. If you can, check before you call. If there is no spare, or it will not hold air, the answer is a tow to a tire shop instead.

sections.heading: Find the key before the truck arrives.
sections.body: If the wheels have locking lug nuts, there is a special key for them, usually in the glove box, the center console, or with the jack and tools under the trunk floor. Without it the wheel cannot come off. Finding it before the driver arrives saves the most time of anything you can do.

sections.heading: A spare is a way to get to a shop.
sections.body: Most spares are compact temporary tires, the narrow ones, and they are not meant for highway speeds or long distances. Check the sidewall for the speed limit printed on it and drive to a tire shop rather than carrying on with your day. If the flat was caused by damage to the wheel itself — a bent rim from a pothole or a curb — mention it, because a spare does not fix a wheel that will not seat properly, and that is a tow rather than a tire change.

faqs.q: What if I do not have a spare?
faqs.a: Then a tire change cannot be done at the roadside, and the answer is a tow to a tire shop. Say so on the call so the right truck is sent the first time.

faqs.q: Can you change a flat on the highway?
faqs.a: Yes, though on a busy highway the safest answer is sometimes to move the car somewhere quieter first. Get as far onto the shoulder as you can, turn on the hazards, and stay clear of traffic while you wait.

pages.heading: Motorcycle towing in Dallas.
pages.intro: Bikes moved on proper straps and wheel chocks, not tied down with whatever happens to be on the truck.
pages.seoTitle: Motorcycle Towing Dallas TX | 24 Hour Towing Dallas
pages.seoDescription: Motorcycle towing in Dallas, Texas. Bikes secured properly for transport after a breakdown or accident, 24 hours a day.

sections.heading: A bike does not tow like a car.
sections.body: A motorcycle cannot be hooked up and pulled. It has to ride on a deck, held upright in a wheel chock and strapped down at points that will not bend a fairing, scratch the tank or compress the forks too far. Done badly, a bike can arrive with more damage than it left with.

sections.heading: Take care of yourself first.
sections.body: If the bike went down, get yourself checked before you think about the motorcycle. Call 911 if anyone is hurt. Once that is handled, a tow can take the bike to a shop, your home, or wherever the insurance adjuster needs to see it.

sections.heading: Size, condition, and where it is.
sections.body: Say what the bike is — a sport bike, a cruiser, a touring bike or a dirt bike — and whether it is upright or down. Mention damage to the wheels or forks, because a bike that will not roll straight needs to be loaded differently. If it has hard bags or a top case, say so; they change where straps can go.

sections.heading: What happens to your helmet and bags.
sections.body: Riders often forget that they are stranded with the bike and everything on it. Helmets, jackets and anything in the saddlebags can usually travel with the motorcycle, but secure them or take them with you rather than assuming they will be fine loose on the deck. If you need a ride as well as a tow, ask about it when you call, because there is not always room in the cab and it is better to know before the truck leaves than when it arrives.

faqs.q: Will my motorcycle be scratched or damaged in the tow?
faqs.a: It should not be. The bike rides upright on a flat deck, held in a wheel chock and strapped at points that do not press on paint or fairings. Tell dispatch about any existing damage so it is known before loading.

faqs.q: Can you tow a motorcycle that will not roll?
faqs.a: Yes, though it is a different loading job. Say on the call if a wheel is locked or bent, or the forks are damaged, so the driver comes prepared.

faqHeading: What people ask before they call.

faqs.q: What decides the cost of a tow?
faqs.a: Mainly the distance, the type of vehicle, and how hard it is to reach. A car on a driveway and the same car nosed into a ditch are different jobs, because one is a hookup and the other is a recovery. Time of day can matter too. Ask for the figure when you call, with the vehicle and the location in front of you — that is when it can actually be answered.

faqs.q: Are you licensed and insured?
faqs.a: Yes — drivers are licensed and the operation is insured. It is a fair thing to ask before handing over a vehicle, and worth asking of anyone you call, because a tow means someone else takes custody of something valuable of yours for the length of the journey.

faqs.q: Are you really open at 3am?
faqs.a: Yes. Dispatch runs 24 hours a day, every day, which is the whole point of the number. Breakdowns and accidents do not keep business hours, and a towing company that only answers in the daytime is not much use at the moment you need one.

faqs.q: What should I tell dispatch when I call?
faqs.a: Four things get the right truck moving: where you are, what you are driving, what is wrong with it, and where you want it taken. Cross streets, a mile marker or an exit number beat a street name on a highway. If the car will not shift out of park, or the keys are gone, say so on the call rather than when the driver arrives.

faqs.q: Should I wait in the vehicle?
faqs.a: On a highway, no. If you can get out safely on the side away from traffic and wait behind a barrier, that is the safer place to be — a stopped vehicle on a shoulder is a target. Put the hazards on, and if you have cones or triangles, set them out behind. On a quiet residential street, staying in the car with the doors locked is usually fine.

faqs.q: Can you tow a car that will not start or has no keys?
faqs.a: Yes. Cars that will not start, will not shift, have a flat battery, or have seized brakes get moved regularly — that is most of the work. Tell dispatch on the call so the right equipment comes out the first time. A car that cannot roll needs a different approach from one that can.

faqs.q: Can you take it to my own mechanic?
faqs.a: Yes. It is your vehicle and your choice of destination — a shop, a dealership, your home, or a body shop after an accident. Have the address ready when you call. If you are not sure where you want it yet, say so, because that changes what the driver needs to know.

faqs.q: Do I need the title to have a junk car removed?
faqs.a: In most cases you need to show you own the vehicle before it can be taken away, and the title is the usual way to do that. Rules vary by situation, so it is worth raising on the call rather than at the curb. Also mention if the car is behind a gate, blocked in, or has no wheels, because that changes the equipment.

faqs.q: What areas do you cover?
faqs.a: Dallas and the surrounding metro, including Arlington and the neighboring suburbs. If you are near the edge of that, ask when you call rather than assuming — the answer depends partly on where the vehicle is going as well as where it is now.
